$comment: The short list of names BETA-Foundations does not define, kept in one file so it
is obvious what is real and what is scaffolding. Everything here either aliases a
real primitive — so the value still comes from Figma — or is page furniture the
design system has no opinion on (content width, sidebar width, column minimums).
A few entries are genuinely missing from the design system rather than out of scope:
border widths, the focus-ring width and the focus glow. Figma defines
color.focus-ring but neither a thickness nor a soft shadow for it, so the glow is
mixed from that colour here and follows it into dark mode. The glow IS the focus
state on a field — a halo, not a second edge — so it carries a spread ring and a
blur rather than the hairline it used to sit under.
This file also carries the density mapping. Density is not a Figma mode: the
export ships input.default.* and input.compact.* as separate paths, so the two
sets below map them onto one set of names that components can reference.
The preview.* names are the prototype's own furniture: the device frame the
Ansicht switch shows the form in. 390x844 is the phone the mobile mode of the
export is meant for, and it sits below the 640px breakpoint with room to spare.
Density: the default branch of the export's input.* tokens.
field.radius is the one deliberate departure: the export puts
input.default.radius at radius.lg (8px), and the default density uses
radius.md (4px) instead, matching the compact branch. It points at the
primitive rather than at input.compact.radius so the two densities stay
independent — a change to compact must not drag the default with it.
Consequence: a change to input.default.radius in BETA-Foundations will no
longer land here. Delete this override to put the field back on the export.

tokens.field.gap.label: {spacing.1}
tokens.focus.glow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-focus-ring) 16%, transparent), 0 2px 12px 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-focus-ring) 26%, transparent)

$comment: The export has only two surface levels — background.page and
background.surface — and the design needs a third for the section cards.
The greys that fit are held only by state tokens (background.hover /
background.active), which would be wrong to borrow, so the card surface is
declared here instead. Light is one step off the white page (neutral.100) —
the quietest grey the ramp offers that still reads as a fill; dark is two
steps up from the neutral.950 page, which is what background.raised already is.
Power-user density: the export's input.compact.* branch. 32px is the
smallest field here and still clears the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 target.
